site.name: Navish Kumar
site.title: Research Portfolio
site.subtitle: A minimal map of ideas, methods, and progression.
site.statement: I treat research as designed intellectual work: each project is a component in a longer argument about how to model complex systems with precision and care.

arcs.name: Geometry for Reliable Inference
arcs.thesis: Design optimization geometry so variational inference is not only fast in practice, but provably stable.

arcs.name: AI for Urban Logistics Transition
arcs.thesis: Use spatial data and predictive modeling to make low-emission delivery systems operationally credible.

arcs.name: Spectral Methods in Gain Graphs
arcs.thesis: Connect graph structure, balance, and eigenvalue bounds to characterize stability in signed and gain networks.

arcs.name: Harm and Counterspeech Dynamics
arcs.thesis: Study how antagonistic and protective speech behaviors co-evolve in social systems.

arcs.name: Emerging Directions
arcs.thesis: New work appears here until curated into a dedicated arc.

08ZZubdj9fEC.summary: Establishes convergence guarantees for natural-gradient variational inference through a square-root covariance parameterization.
08ZZubdj9fEC.contribution: Bridges practical natural-gradient performance with theoretical guarantees under concave log-likelihood settings.

738O_yMBCRsC.summary: Models delivery performance across urban micro-regions to evaluate where cargo-bike logistics can outperform van-based fleets.
738O_yMBCRsC.contribution: Combines H3 spatial partitioning and OpenStreetMap features to forecast service-time dynamics by neighborhood context.

WbkHhVStYXYC.summary: Derives lower and upper bounds for extremal eigenvalues of gain Laplacians, linking spectral behavior to graph frustration.
WbkHhVStYXYC.contribution: Extends spectral analysis for complex-unit gain graphs and clarifies how balance constraints shape eigen-structure.

OU6Ihb5iCvQC.summary: Introduces normalized Laplacians for gain graphs and studies spectral implications of balancedness and bipartiteness.
OU6Ihb5iCvQC.contribution: Builds a foundational spectral toolkit and extends interlacing results to gain-graph settings.

SP6oXDckpogC.summary: Analyzes interaction patterns between hate and counter users on Twitter, with a released paired-user dataset.
SP6oXDckpogC.contribution: Shows how counterspeech strategies differ by community while exposing behavioral and linguistic asymmetries in hate accounts.
